free_tier.stated: Stated as 'Unlock up to $10k of credits to be used on Modal to supercharge your project' for 'Graduate students, labs, and researchers'; the form behind the page's grant link states 'We are not currently running a credit grant program', so no award is open.
free_tier.notes: the page publishes a ceiling ('up to $10k'), not an award floor and not a number of awards; no expiry is stated on the pages read

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a credit balance, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: the ceiling that matters is the grant amount, recorded in free_tier

retention.stated: not applicable: the grant is a credit balance rather than stored bytes; no expiry is stated on the pages read

egress.terms: Charged to the workspace that spends the credit: 'Starting October 1, 2026, Modal charges for network egress.', with 1 TiB included per billing cycle on Starter and '$0.04 per GiB' beyond…
egress.free_allowance: 1 TiB per billing cycle on Starter
egress.price_per_tb: USD 0.04 per GiB beyond the included volume

interface_detail: the programme's page names 'Modal's developer-first Python API'; the API endpoint itself is not stated on the pages read
tooling: Modal's Python SDK over the platform API that a credit is spent through; the grant is requested through a web form that asks for a name, an academic email and a lab or group website
chaining: A grant would be spent inside the same Starter workspace as the platform's USD 30 monthly compute allowance, on the same B200 and H100 pool the page offers 'without requesting quota', so it would extend that recurring allowance rather than replace it; while the window is shut and restricted to eligible institutions, the USD 30 allowance is the only live route into the pool.

limits.value: the grant is limited to 'Researchers from eligible institutions who are submitting work to select AI/ML conferences (ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS)', the form requires an academic email, a name and a lab or group website, and it states 'We are not currently running a credit grant program.'
a payment method on file is required to use the platform at all: 'Note that you must have a payment method on file in order to use Modal.'

limits_note: the grant has no published number of awards, no award floor and no expiry; the only number is the 'up to $10k' ceiling, decided case by case
binding_note: identity decides it twice: the grant is restricted to researchers at eligible institutions and its window is shut, so no application can be filed from an unaffiliated account, and the platform itself requires a payment method before GPU time runs. No quota can be spent while neither gate opens.

identity_cost.detail: the grant form asks for an 'Academic email', a name and a 'Lab / group website', and the page limits credits to 'Researchers from eligible institutions who are submitting work to select AI/ML conferences (ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS)'; the platform account that would spend a credit also needs a payment method: 'Note that you must have a payment method on file in order to use Modal.' A phone number or an ID document is not requested. Country: none stated.

reliability_note: the programme is advertised but not running: the page keeps its 'up to $10k' line while the form behind the 'Academic credits form' link states no grant is open, so the only route a reader reaches is a mailing-list form.

evidence.proved: the academics page advertises 'up to $10k of credits' as the programme's headline benefit
evidence.quote: Unlock up to $10k of credits to be used on Modal to supercharge your project

evidence.proved: the page's only call to action is a mailing-list sign-up, not an application form
evidence.quote: Sign up to hear about our grant programs

evidence.proved: the form behind the page's 'Academic credits form' states that no credit grant programme is running and collects interest for future ones
evidence.quote: We are not currently running a credit grant program. Please fill out the form below if you'd like to be informed about future programs.

evidence.proved: eligibility is an eligible institution plus a submission to ICLR, ICML or NeurIPS; the form is the 'Modal for Academics mailing list'
evidence.quote: Researchers from eligible institutions who are submitting work to select AI/ML conferences (ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS) can get compute credits on Modal to support specific submissions.

evidence.proved: the form's fields are an academic email, a name and a lab or group website, all marked required in the form definition
the second required field is labelled 'Academic email', so a personal address is not what the form asks for
the pricing page repeats the offer and its audience: graduate students, labs and researchers, up to $10k
evidence.quote: Graduate students, labs, and researchers can get up to $10k free compute credits on Modal

evidence.proved: a payment method on file is a precondition of using the platform the credit is spent on
evidence.quote: Note that you must have a payment method on file in order to use Modal.

evidence.proved: Starter includes 1 TiB of network egress a billing cycle and charges USD 0.04 per GiB beyond it
no credit grant programme is running and the form is the route to be informed about future programmes

notes: The advertised figure is the only published number: no award floor, no number of awards and no expiry appear on the pages read, so the quota is a ceiling decided case by case rather than a quota a user can plan on. What would reverse the finding: a form that accepts an application, and an eligibility line that does not require an institution. The Starter plan's USD 30 monthly compute allowance is a separate, live offer of the same provider.
